text:
alex: Heads up — since the nodepool rolling update at ~08:02 UTC we have ~40% of GPU nodes in eu-west3 reporting NotReady/NoSchedule. Pods got evicted and workloads spilled to the CPU pool. Cluster-autoscaler started spinning up more nodes.

jamie: saw the alerts, thanks. Any driver/device-plugin logs yet?

alex: grabbing logs: `kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin -c plugin` shows repeated `failed to initialize NVML: -1` and `device plugin handshake timeout`; plugin exits and restarts. `kubectl describe node` shows `kernel: udev queued event` errors and `nvidia: module bind failed`.

sarah: timeline — did we roll images/kernels?

alex: node image rollout started 08:00 with kernel 5.15 + nvidia driver 520. Reverting a single node to old image makes device-plugin healthy there. Suspect a race: if many nodes boot at once, udev/module binding delays cause the plugin init to time out.

tori: could be startup concurrency. Our NodePool had surge=100% for the rollout and cluster-autoscaler also scaled aggressively, so many GPU nodes hit the cluster simultaneously.

jamie: infra-bot: incident please.

infra-bot: Created incident INC-2026-423 and paged oncall.

sarah: short-term mitigations: reduce nodepool max surge to 1, rollback the node image to previous stable, cordon+drain affected nodes in small batches.

alex: doing cordon/drain in batches of 5. Also applied a temporary patch to the device-plugin DaemonSet to add randomized init sleep so nodes don't hammer the driver all at once.

alex: example jitter I applied:
```
initContainers:
- name: jitter
  image: busybox
  command: ['sh','-c','sleep $((RANDOM % 45))']
```

tori: good short-term. Can we add retries in the plugin so it waits for `/dev/nvidia0` instead of failing fast? Also change autoscaler flags: increase `--scale-down-delay-after-add` to avoid churn.

jamie: also suggest an annotation `gpu-init-complete` set by a small readiness job so we know nodes that finished driver/udev setup before scheduling GPU pods.

sarah: long-term: add preflight validation in the node image bake that exercises kernel+driver ABI matrix, bake in driver modules, and add jitter to rolling update logic. Consider pre-warming driver artifacts on boot.

alex: I'll open a PR with three items: 1) jitter initContainer in device-plugin chart, 2) plugin retry loop that checks for device nodes with exponential backoff, 3) cluster-autoscaler flag changes and nodepool surge default adjustments.

tori: linking related doc: https://internal.redwood/devices/kernel-nvidia-matrix — add kernel-driver compatibility tests to CI.

jamie: what about cost impact from the spillover?

alex: CPU pools autoscaled and extra nodes ran for ~3 hours — rough estimate $2.5k for the incident window. Will attach billing snapshot.

sarah: I'll file a cost incident and notify finance.

infra-bot: INC-2026-423 updated: mitigations applied, RCA pending.

alex: RCA note (working): root cause is startup concurrency combined with a kernel/driver timing mismatch that delays udev/module binding; device-plugin had tight timeouts and failed early, which resulted in nodes being marked NotReady and subsequent pod evictions.

tori: will review the PR and schedule a config rollback window. Thanks all.

jamie: :thumbsup:
